info.title: bitHuman
info.description:
Real-time, lip-synced AI avatars: audio in, talking video out — on
the cloud, on your own hardware, or in the browser. This is the REST
contract; the guides, the SDKs and the CLI are on
[docs.bithuman.ai](https://docs.bithuman.ai).

All endpoints are relative to `https://api.bithuman.ai` and
require an `api-secret` header.
[Get an API secret →](https://www.bithuman.ai/developer/api-keys)

This machine-readable spec covers the developer surface. Two groups
are documented only in the markdown guides, not here:
[organizations](https://docs.bithuman.ai/api/organizations)
(`/v2/organizations*`, `/v2/agents/{agent_code}/share-org`) and the
[Realtime WebSocket relay](https://docs.bithuman.ai/api/realtime)
(`wss://api.bithuman.ai/v1/realtime`). Purely internal / infrastructure routes —
webhook receivers, `/func_*` generation internals, health/telemetry,
and realtime session plumbing — are excluded entirely: they are not
part of the public developer contract and may change without notice.

post.description:
Verify that your API secret is valid and your account is active.

Always returns HTTP 200. Inspect the `valid` field in the body
to determine outcome — invalid or missing credentials yield
`{"valid": false}` rather than a 401. The secret goes in the
`api-secret` header; a secret sent as `Authorization: Bearer` is
not read and also yields `{"valid": false}`.

post.description:
Create a new avatar agent from a text prompt, with optional image
and audio assets. Poll `/v1/agent/status/{agent_id}` to check
progress.

**Agent creation is image-only.** Provide a portrait `image` (or let
the prompt generate one) — bitHuman generates a **10-second
identity video internally**, authored to loop without a seam (its
first and last frames match). A `video` field is rejected with
`400 VIDEO_INPUT_NOT_SUPPORTED` before anything is billed.

**Selecting a model.** Always send `model`: `essence-2`,
`expression-2`, `auto`, `essence-1` or `expression-1`. An omitted
`model` creates an `expression-1` agent. A model outside your plan
returns `403 PLAN_REQUIRED`.

**Creation time depends on the model** (the second-generation models
train a per-identity model, so don't apply a 5-minute client
timeout):

| `model` | identity input | creation time |
|---|---|---|
| `essence-2` | image (or generated from prompt); a 10-second identity video is generated internally | about 2–2.5 h |
| `expression-2` | image (or generated from prompt) | about 2–2.5 h |
| `auto` | image or prompt (classified automatically) | as the routed model (`essence-2` or `expression-2`) |
| `essence-1` | image (or generated from prompt) | under 15 min |
| `expression-1` (the default when `model` is omitted) | image (or generated from prompt) | about 1 min |

Times run from this call to `status: "ready"` on
`GET /v1/agent/status/{agent_id}`. They are a typical range, not a
guarantee, and individual runs can take longer: size timeouts in
hours for the second-generation models.

**Picking the right family** ([Choosing a model](https://docs.bithuman.ai/models#choosing-a-model)):
`essence-2` for a real person; `expression-2` for a cartoon,
stylized, animal, creature or robot character. Send
`model: "auto"` to apply this rule automatically — the platform
classifies your input and records the recommended model either way.

**Subject requirement:** every model except `expression-2` needs a
clear, **real human face**: `essence-2`, `essence-1` and
`expression-1` (also when `model` is omitted). The input is
classified before anything is billed; a cartoon, stylized
character, animal, creature or robot, or a photo with no face
found, is rejected with `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH` (nothing
charged) — use `expression-2` for those characters, or send
`model: "auto"` to route automatically.

Failures during generation surface as `status: "failed"` with an
`error_message` on the status endpoint, and the creation credits
are automatically refunded.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A unique client-generated key (e.g. a UUID). Retrying with the same key returns the original response instead of starting a second billed job. Keys are retained for 24 hours.

prompt.description: System prompt / personality for the agent. If omitted, a random default is used.
prompt.example: You are a friendly fitness coach who motivates users.

image.description: URL to a face image for avatar appearance. For the best likeness use a photo with one clear figure, a neutral expression, facing the camera, a relaxed pose, and no occlusion of the face. Every model except Expression 2 needs a real human face (otherwise 422 `MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`), and Essence 2 needs the face clearly in frame (otherwise 422 `IMAGE_FACE_UNSUITABLE`), before any charge.

audio.description: URL to audio for voice cloning.

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio for the generated identity image and driver video. `16:9` landscape (default), `9:16` portrait, `1:1` square. Images are generated at 1080p on this ratio.

transparency.description: When `true`, the identity image is generated on a solid green-screen background (chroma-key friendly) so the avatar can be embedded transparently — the character itself never uses green. Leave `false` for a normal scene background.

framing.description: `portrait` (default) frames head-and-shoulders; `full_body` shows the full figure including the feet — use it for kiosk / standing-avatar layouts.

agent_id.description: Custom agent identifier. Auto-generated if omitted.

duration.description: **Deprecated — omit it.** The internally generated identity video is 10 seconds (authored to loop without a seam); this parameter is ignored.

model.description:
Which model to create. Always send it; if omitted, an `expression-1` agent is created (250 credits). A model outside your plan returns `403 PLAN_REQUIRED`. The bare family names `essence` and `expression` are still accepted for older integrations (they select the version-1 model); new code should send a full model name.

**`essence-2`** is the second-generation Essence model for photorealistic people — one 500-credit creation that runs everywhere from on-device (CPU / Apple silicon) up to cloud GPU. **`expression-2`** is the second-generation expression engine — audio-driven real-time avatar video from a single photo (creation trains a per-identity model — about 2 hours, as does `essence-2`; see the creation-time table above). **`auto`** classifies your input (the image if provided, else the prompt): a photorealistic person routes to `essence-2`, a cartoon / animal / creature / robot to `expression-2`. Retired engine names return `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Identity inputs and creation times differ per model — see the endpoint description table and [Compare models](https://docs.bithuman.ai/models).

version.description: **Older form — send a full model name in `model` instead.** With a bare family name in `model` (`essence` or `expression`), `v1` selects the first-generation model and `v2` the second-generation one. Ignored when `model` is a full model name or `auto`.

400.description: Body failed validation — malformed JSON, an invalid / retired `model` value (`VALIDATION_ERROR` — the message lists the accepted model names), or a `video` input (`VIDEO_INPUT_NOT_SUPPORTED` — agent creation is image-only; the 10-second identity video is generated internally so it loops without a seam; never send `video`). Rejected before dispatch; no credits charged.

error.message: Invalid model 'my-model'; must be one of: auto, essence, essence-1, essence-2, expression, expression-1, expression-2

Agent creation is image-only. Provide a portrait `image`; bitHuman generates a 10-second idle/driver video internally so it loops without a seam (first frame == last frame). Video input is not accepted for any model (essence-1, expression-1, essence-2, expression-2).

402.description: Insufficient credits. Creation is billed **per model** — `expression-2` costs 2000 credits; `essence-2` costs 500; `auto` bills the routed model's rate (500 or 2000); the v1 families (`essence-1`, `expression-1`) cost 250. Returns error code `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`; top up at the error's `topup_url`.

403.description: `PLAN_REQUIRED` — the model is not in your plan (the message names the plan; contact sales), or a Free account, which cannot create agents. `AGENT_LIMIT_REACHED` — a new agent would pass your plan's agent limit; existing agents keep working. Both carry `upgrade_url`; nothing is charged.

plan_required.summary: A Free account creating an agent

error.message: Creating agents starts at the Creator plan. Upgrade at https://www.bithuman.ai/pricing.
Your Creator plan includes 7 agents and you have 7. Existing agents keep working; delete one or upgrade at https://www.bithuman.ai/pricing to create more.

422.description: `MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH` — a creation for a model that needs a real human face (`essence-2`, `essence-1`, `expression-1`, or `model` omitted) whose input is a cartoon, stylized character, animal, creature or robot, or a photo with no face found. The classifier runs on the image if provided, else the prompt, **before anything is billed** and before any agent row is created. Use `expression-2` for those subjects, or `model: "auto"` (which never rejects — it routes instead). A classifier outage never blocks creation (the gate fails open). `IMAGE_FACE_UNSUITABLE` — an Essence 2 creation whose photo has a face too small in frame, or several similar-sized faces; upload a closer photo of one person. Nothing is charged.

error.message: Essence 2 needs a clear, real human face, and this image looks like a cartoon or stylized character. Use Expression 2, which animates any character: cartoons, animals, robots and stylized art. Nothing was charged.

503.description: `MODEL_NOT_YET_AVAILABLE` — the requested second-generation model (`essence-2`, `expression-2`, or `auto`, which routes only to them) can't accept creations right now. Essence 2 and Expression 2 have been generally available since their July 10, 2026 launch, so this is a rare, temporary operational pause — returned **before any dispatch or charge**. The v1 families (`essence-1`, `expression-1`) always work; retry the v2 model shortly.

error.message: expression-2 isn't available for generation yet. Specify 'essence-1' or 'expression-1' to generate now.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
curl https://api.bithuman.ai/v1/agent/status/A95SXN5716 \
  -H "api-secret: $BITHUMAN_API_SECRET"
# poll every 5 s until data.status is "ready" (or "failed").
# "success" is a STEP marker written mid-run — not terminal unless progress == 1.0

get.description:
Poll this endpoint to check generation progress. Status values:
`processing`, `generating`, `completed`, `success` (all intermediate);
`ready` (terminal success); `failed` (terminal error).

**Keep polling past `generating`, `completed` and `success`** — those
are intermediate states, not terminal. `completed` can appear early
(even around ~5% `progress`), and `success` is a STEP-level marker the
voice/image and video steps each write (~20% and ~45% `progress`), so
do not stop on either. Only `ready` and `failed` mean polling should
stop — or `success` when `progress` has also reached `1.0`.

`current_step` reports the pipeline stage: `payment` (~2%) →
`persona` (5–15%) → `voice_image` (~20%) → `video` (~45%, the
internally generated 10-second identity video — models that need
one) → `lip_sync` (70–99%, the
model-specific identity step — training/distillation for
`expression-2` / `essence-2`, so the longest stage) → `done`
(100%). A rare `essence-1` path reports `awaiting_face_marking`
(~35%).

Recommended polling interval: 5 seconds. Size your overall timeout to
the model: minutes for the first-generation engines, **hours** for
both second-generation ones (about 2–2.5 hours from creation to `ready`).

**`ready` does not yet mean downloadable.** The agent can be launched
and embedded as soon as it reports `ready`, but the downloadable
model file is published separately, shortly afterwards. Until it is,
`GET /v1/agent/{code}/model/download` answers
`404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY` — a retryable code, not a failure. It
can take a few minutes after `ready`; poll the download while it
answers `404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY`.

200.description: Agent status. `data` is the agent's full record — the same shape `GET /v1/agent/{code}` returns.

get.description: Retrieve full details for an agent by its code.

post.summary: Update an agent's prompt or providers
post.description:
Update an existing agent's system prompt, its provider selection, or
both. The agent must already exist (use `POST /v1/agent/generate` to
create one). Send at least one of `system_prompt` and `providers` — a
body with neither is rejected `400 MISSING_PARAM`.

**An agent's `name` cannot be set here, and cannot be set at
creation either.** Names are generated from the agent's prompt and
portrait. A body whose only field is `name` changes nothing and
returns `400 MISSING_PARAM`; sending `name` alongside `system_prompt`
updates the prompt and ignores the name.

schema.description: Send `system_prompt`, `providers`, or both. Any other field is ignored.

system_prompt.description: New system prompt for the agent.
system_prompt.example: You are a professional sales assistant.

providers.description: Which provider each capability uses for this agent. Give a capability `"default"` to use the platform's own provider, or an object `{"mode": "custom", "provider_id": "<id>"}` to point it at one you registered yourself. The patch is merged, so a capability you omit keeps its current selection. An unknown capability name, an unusable selection, or a `provider_id` that is not registered on your account is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` at write time with the reason — nothing is stored half-configured.

400.description: Nothing to update, or a `providers` patch that cannot be stored. `MISSING_PARAM` — the body carried neither `system_prompt` nor `providers` (an empty body, or one whose only field is `name`). `VALIDATION_ERROR` — malformed JSON, or a `providers` patch naming an unknown capability, an unusable selection, or a `provider_id` that is not registered on your account.

error.message: Nothing to update — send 'system_prompt' and/or 'providers'

unregistered_provider.summary: A provider id this account has not registered

error.message: provider_id 'does-not-exist' is not registered on this account

delete.description:
Permanently delete an agent you own. Stored assets are cleaned up
best-effort; usage history is retained. Deleting a missing or
non-owned agent returns 404.

artifact_cleanup.description: How far the removal of the agent's stored assets has got. `pending` means the delete has been accepted and the files are still being removed in the background — the agent is already gone from `GET /v1/agents` and every route answers `404` for its code.

billing_history.description: What happened to this agent's billing records. The per-call rows go with the agent; the account-level summaries they roll up into are retained, so your invoice does not change.

post.description:
Send text for the avatar to speak aloud. With `room_id` it goes to that
one session; without it, to every deliverable session of the agent.
The agent must be in at least one active LiveKit room.

message.description: Text for the avatar to speak.

room_id.description: Target a specific room (optional, defaults to all active rooms).

delivered_to_rooms.description: Number of active rooms that received the message.

rooms.description: Room ids that received the message.

rooms_skipped.description: Live rooms with no agent worker attached, so not delivered to.

rooms_failed.description: Rooms the publish was attempted on and failed.

get.description:
The sessions this agent has open now. Pass a returned `room_id` to
/speak or /add-context to address ONE session instead of broadcasting.
`deliverable` is false when the room is live but no agent worker is
attached — /speak on such a room returns 404.

created_at.description: LiveKit room creation time, Unix seconds.

deliverable.description: Whether an agent worker is attached and /speak would reach it.

matched_by.description: How the room was bound to this agent.

post.summary: Add a model to an existing agent
post.description:
Add an avatar model to an agent you already created — no need to
re-create the agent or regenerate its persona/voice/image. The agent
must be in the `ready` state (else `409 AGENT_NOT_READY`).

| model | what happens | prerequisites | credits | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expression-1` | **immediate enablement** — the v1 engine drives the agent's existing image + voice at runtime; nothing is trained | stored image + voice + real-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | **0** | immediate (this response) |
| `expression-2` | trains the per-identity Expression 2 model from the stored image | stored image | 2000 | the same training an `expression-2` creation runs — about 2–2.5 h (see [creation times](#operation/generateAgent)) |
| `essence-2` | trains Essence 2 from the agent's stored identity video (generated internally at creation) | stored identity video (else `422`) + photorealistic-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | 500 | the same training an `essence-2` creation runs — about 2–2.5 h (see [creation times](#operation/generateAgent)) |
| `essence-1` | builds the v1 `.imx` from the agent's stored identity video (or generates one internally from the stored image) | stored identity video or image + real-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | 250 | ~10–20 min |

Asynchronous adds return `status: "processing"` — poll
[`GET /v1/agent/status/{agent_id}`](#tag/Agent-Generation/operation/getAgentStatus)
until `supported_models` contains the new family. Charges are refunded
automatically if the add fails; re-POSTing the same model never
double-charges, and returns `status: "ready"` with `credits: 0` once
the model already exists.

model.description: The model to add. Anything else returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` listing these options.

200.description: Model added (`status: "ready"` — immediate or already available) or the add started (`status: "processing"` — poll supported_models).

credits.description: Credits charged for this add (0 for immediate enablement or when already available).

supported_models.description: The agent's launchable model families at response time.

400.description: Invalid `model` (the message lists the addable options).

409.description: `AGENT_NOT_READY` — the agent is still generating or failed; models can only be added to a ready agent.

422.description: `MODEL_PREREQUISITE_MISSING` — the agent lacks a stored asset the model needs (e.g. `essence-2` needs the agent's stored identity video — generated internally by Essence creations, never uploaded), or `MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH` — `essence-2`, `essence-1` and `expression-1` need a real human face, and the agent's subject is a cartoon, stylized character, animal, creature or robot, or its photo has no face found (use `expression-2`). Nothing is charged.

503.description: `MODEL_NOT_YET_AVAILABLE` — adding a second-generation model (`essence-2`, `expression-2`) can't be dispatched right now. Both models have been generally available since the July 10, 2026 launch, so this is a rare, temporary operational pause. Rejected before any charge — retry shortly. Adding the v1 models always works.

x-codeSamples.label: cURL
x-codeSamples.source:
# 302 redirect to the artifact — -L follows it, -o names the file
curl -L -o "A17ZTB0222.imx" \
  "https://api.bithuman.ai/v1/agent/A17ZTB0222/model/download?model=expression-2" \
  -H "api-secret: $BITHUMAN_API_SECRET"
# → A17ZTB0222.imx  (add ?redirect=false for the URL as JSON)

get.description:
Download the generated model file for an agent you own. The family
defaults to the agent's own model; override with `?model=<family>`
(canonical names, legacy names, and runtime tier slugs all fold onto
their family). Artifact per family:

| family | artifact |
|---|---|
| `essence-1` | `<code>.imx` (the portable IMX container) |
| `essence-2` | `<CODE>.imx` — the standard Essence 2 artifact (unified IMX container; size is per identity — read `Content-Length` rather than assuming a figure; **licensed weights** — renders locally in the CLI, the Python SDK, the Android library and the Swift `Essence2` product, and the first local play checks the license with the cloud, so it needs a sign-in: https://docs.bithuman.ai/platforms/cli/voice#platform-notes). |
| `expression-2` | `<code>.avatar` — the same container as `.imx` under a second name (a few early identities use an older format; `bithuman open` reports which) — runs locally on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux x86_64, or in the browser, and is also served on bitHuman's cloud |
| `expression-1` | normally not downloadable (the shared v1 engine renders server-side from the agent's image) → `400 MODEL_NOT_DOWNLOADABLE`; an agent that went through the lip step owns a baked `<code>.imx` and is redirected to it like `essence-1` |

The default response is a **302 redirect** to the artifact — the
public URL for `essence-1`, a **1-hour signed URL** on a private
bucket for the other families — so `curl -L` and browser anchors just
work. Pass `?redirect=false` to get the URL as JSON instead.

**Name the file yourself** (`curl -L -o "<CODE>.imx"`). The redirect
target does not always send a `Content-Disposition` header — the
public `essence-1` URL sends none — so a filename-from-the-header
flag such as `curl -LOJ` silently falls back to the last path segment
of the request URL and writes a file called `download`. With
`?redirect=false` the JSON carries the intended name in `filename`.

The launchability gate doubles as the download gate: a family the
agent can't be launched as (missing from `supported_models`) returns
`409 MODEL_NOT_GENERATED`. A family the agent supports whose artifact
hasn't been published to the download store yet returns
`404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY` — the message says when to retry;
**poll on that code**.

**Every grant is recorded.** A model download costs **0 credits** on
the [pricing table](https://docs.bithuman.ai/pricing) — only
runtime minutes bill — but the grant still writes exactly one usage row
before the URL is issued, under the family's self-hosted pricing code,
and hands you its id in `X-Bithuman-Meter-Id`. The rows show up in
`GET /v1/usage` at 0 credits; they are a record of what you fetched,
not a charge. The order matters both ways: a meter that refuses
(`402`) or fails (`500`) returns no URL at all.

The [bitHuman CLI](https://docs.bithuman.ai/platforms/cli/reference) wraps
this endpoint: `bithuman pull <AGENT_CODE>` downloads the artifact,
recognizes its model family, and prints what to do next.

**Showcase identities need no credential.** The `essence-2` and
`expression-2` identities listed by
[`GET /v1/models/showcase`](#tag/Agent-Management/operation/getShowcaseManifest)
are served to anonymous callers — same 302, same 1-hour signed URL, and
the owner is charged **0 credits**. Every other agent still needs the
`api-secret` header (or `Authorization: Bearer <api-secret | runtime
token>`) and must be owned by the caller; an anonymous request for one
answers `401 MISSING_AUTH`, the same answer an unknown code gets.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Agent code. The agent must be owned by the caller (else 404) — except for the showcase identities in `GET /v1/models/showcase`, which are served with no credential.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Artifact family. Defaults to the agent's own model. The runtime tier slugs (`essence-2-apple`, `essence-2-gpu`, `essence-2-cpu`, `expression-2-gpu`; the older `essence-2-ane` spelling stays accepted) fold onto their family. `essence-2-quality` returns `400`; send `essence-2`. Any other unrecognized value returns the same `400`, listing the downloadable families.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: Fetch ONE on-device model member instead of the whole container. `essence-2` and `expression-2` publish a browser/Android bundle beside the container — a `web_manifest.json` and the members it lists (`combined_fp32.tflite`, `canon.bin`, ...) — and this serves a single one of them, so a browser or an Android runtime pulls only the files it runs. Same entitlement as the container, same 1-hour signed URL, and the URL honours `Range` (`curl -L -r 0-1023` answers `206`, so OkHttp and browsers resume). Pass `web_manifest.json` first to learn the member names. A member of a **public** agent is served to an anonymous caller, like the browser already serves those agents; every other visibility needs the same credential as the container.

parameters.name: plane
parameters.description: Which member set `?member=` names. `essence-2` publishes two — one for browsers and one for Android — and twelve names appear in both of them, `manifest.json` among them. A browser asking for `manifest.json` and a handset asking for `manifest.json` want different files, so for those twelve the request has to say which set it means. Only meaningful alongside `member=`: the container itself has one form, so `plane=` on its own returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, as does any value not listed above. **You can usually leave it out.** A member that appears in only one of the two sets identifies itself — which is why the Android runtime's first call, `member=android_store.v1.json`, resolves with no `plane=` at all. When a name appears in both and the request says nothing, it resolves to the browser set, so every caller written before this parameter behaves exactly as it did.

parameters.name: redirect
parameters.description: Pass `false` to receive the artifact URL as JSON (below) instead of a 302 redirect — for UIs that want to fetch or label first.

200.description: With `?redirect=false` — the artifact URL as JSON.

X-Bithuman-Meter-Id.description: The id of the single `activities` row this grant wrote. Every download is metered BEFORE the URL is issued — a model download costs **0 credits** on the published [pricing table](https://docs.bithuman.ai/pricing), and 0 is a price, not a reason to skip the record. post.description:
Upload images, videos, audio, or documents — by public URL or as
base64. Files are organized by type, and the type is read from the
file's own bytes: `file_type` and the filename extension are both
cross-checked against them, never trusted over them. The response
returns a public URL for the stored file.

file_url.description: Public URL to download the file from.

file_type.description: Optional cross-check, not an override — the stored category always comes from the file's own bytes. Give a value and the bytes must agree with it, or the upload is refused with `415`. `document` and `pdf` are the same category. Any other value is refused with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; omit it, or send `auto`, to let the bytes decide. The filename here comes from the URL's path, and its extension must be one of the supported ones.

file_name.description: Original filename. The extension is required and must be one of the supported ones (see `415`); a name without one is refused.

file_type.description: Optional cross-check, not an override — the stored category always comes from the file's own bytes. Give a value and the bytes must agree with it, or the upload is refused with `415`. `document` and `pdf` are the same category. Any other value is refused with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; omit it, or send `auto`, to let the bytes decide.

file_url.description: Public CDN URL of the uploaded file.

400.description:
One of:

- `DOWNLOAD_FAILED` — `file_url` could not be downloaded:
  unreachable, not publicly readable, or not an ordinary public
  `http(s)` address.
- `VALIDATION_ERROR` — `file_data` was not valid base64, both
  `file_url` and `file_data` were sent, or `file_type` was a value
  this API does not define. The accepted values are `auto`,
  `image`, `video`, `audio`, `document` and `pdf`; anything else is
  refused rather than quietly treated as `auto`, so a typo cannot
  silently change where your file lands.
- `MISSING_PARAM` — neither `file_url` nor `file_data` was sent.

error.message: Invalid file_type 'picture'; must be one of: auto, image, video, audio, document, pdf

413.description:
`FILE_TOO_LARGE` — the file is over the limit for its category:
**10 MB** images, **100 MB** video, **25 MB** audio and documents.
The category is read from the file's own bytes, so the limit that
applies is the one for what the file actually is.

error.message: file is 31 MB; the limit for image is 10 MB

415.description:
`UNSUPPORTED_TYPE` — this API will not store the file. Four things
raise it:

- **The bytes are not a supported type.** Supported: JPEG, PNG,
  GIF, WebP, BMP · MP4, MOV, WebM, AVI, WMV, FLV, Matroska ·
  MP3, WAV, FLAC, AAC, OGG, M4A · PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint,
  RTF and plain text.
- **The bytes contradict `file_type`.** Sending
  `file_type: "image"` with a text file is refused here rather than
  stored under the wrong category.
- **The filename extension is not one of the supported ones.** For
  a base64 upload that is `file_name`; for a URL upload it is the
  last path segment of `file_url`. A name with no extension, or
  one like `.exe` or `.sh`, is refused.
- **The file would run in a browser.** SVG, HTML and any text
  carrying a script are refused outright: an uploaded file is
  served from a public address, and a file that executes there
  would run as if it came from us.

get.description:
The catalogue of **Essence 2** and **Expression 2** showcase identities
whose model weights anyone may download — no api-secret, no account.

Each entry's `url` is
[`GET /v1/agent/{code}/model/download`](#tag/Agent-Management/operation/downloadAgentModel),
which answers a **302** to a 1-hour signed URL for anonymous callers
too. The grant is still recorded (one usage row) and costs the agent's
owner **0 credits** — an anonymous download is free or refused, never
billed to the owner.

The list is generated from the download route's own admission
predicate, so a code listed here is a code the route serves: an
`essence-2` or `expression-2` identity that is ready, listed in the
agent gallery, owns its own artifact, and whose owner has authorised
anonymous distribution of the weights. Agents that are merely public in
the gallery are **not** here — being viewable is a different permission
from the weights being distributable.

The shape is the bitHuman CLI's manifest v2; `bithuman list` and
`bithuman pull` read this catalogue.

**Performance.** The reply carries no frame rates.
`note_performance` maps each family in the catalogue to the
[performance page](https://docs.bithuman.ai/performance), where the frame rates are
measured and published for every device.

`sha256` is deliberately empty: no content digest is recorded for these
objects yet, and the CLI skips verification on an empty value rather
than failing. Verify `size` and the file itself (`bithuman open`)
instead.

Throttled per IP; the reply is cached for 60 seconds.

post.summary: Mint a scoped runtime token for one agent
post.description:
Exchange your API secret, **server-side**, for a 1-hour token bound to a
single `agent_code` — so a browser, a phone app or any other client you
do not fully control never holds your master secret.

This is the credential the on-device paths accept. It works as
`Authorization: Bearer <scoped_token>` on
[the model download route](#operation/downloadAgentModel), including
the `?member=` fetch the browser and Android runtimes use.

The scope is real: presenting the token for a **different** agent code
answers `404`, exactly like a code you do not own. It expires in one
hour and is not refreshable — mint another.

**LiveKit plugin.** With `"scope": "livekit-cloud"` this mints the token
to pass to `livekit-plugins-bithuman` as `api_secret` instead of your API
secret. The plugin writes that value into LiveKit room attributes, where
every participant can read it. This token can only start this agent's
cloud avatar session. It is also bound to `room_name` and `livekit_url`
when you send them, and it bills your account. For another agent, room
or LiveKit server it answers `403`. It cannot download the model or call
any other endpoint. See [LiveKit integration](/platforms/livekit).

Call this from your server. Never ship the api-secret this endpoint
consumes to a client.

scope.description: `livekit-cloud` mints the launch-only token for the LiveKit plugin's cloud mode. Omit it for the runtime token described above.

room_name.description: `livekit-cloud` only. Binds the token to this LiveKit room.

livekit_url.description: `livekit-cloud` only. Binds the token to this LiveKit server. It must be the URL the plugin connects to.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds; one hour from minting.

post.description:
Render a talking-video (mp4) from **your audio**, driven by one of
your agents.

**Two modes:**
- **Async (default)** — returns immediately with a `job_id`; poll
  [`GET /v1/video/{job_id}`](#operation/getTalkingVideo) for the finished
  video. Use this for anything but the shortest clips — renders can take a
  while, so you don't want to hold the connection.
- **Sync** — set `wait: true` (or `?wait=true`). The call blocks until the
  render finishes (up to ~90s) and returns the `video_url` directly in this
  response. If the render is still running at that cap you get the async
  response (`status: processing`) instead — just poll the `job_id`.

**Input:** your own audio. `audio_url` (a hosted WAV/MP3: a recording, or
the output of any text-to-speech tool) drives the render directly.

The output is a public CDN URL. `essence-2` renders at
**1080p** by default (1080×1920 portrait or 1920×1080 landscape, matching
the source orientation and capped at the source's long side);
`expression-2` renders at its native 416×720. Limits: max **120 seconds**
of output.

parameters.description: Optional. A unique client-generated key (e.g. a UUID). Retrying with the same key returns the original response instead of starting a second billed job. Keys are retained for 24 hours.

Avatar engine. `essence-1` (2 credits/min) and
`expression-1` (4 credits/min) are the first-generation models,
still supported. `expression-2` (4 credits/min) and `essence-2`

wait.description: Sync toggle. `false` (default) returns a `job_id` immediately (async — poll for the result). `true` blocks until the render finishes (up to ~90s) and returns the finished `video_url` in this response; if it exceeds the cap you get `status: processing` + a `job_id` to poll. `?wait=true` as a query parameter also works.

post.summary: Live key check for a self-hosted runtime
post.description:
The bitHuman SDKs, the CLI and the plugins call this for you when a
self-hosted session starts and while it runs; you call it only if you
build your own runtime. Deleting a key in the dashboard stops a running
self-hosted session at its next check.

A runtime treats the three answers differently:

| status | meaning | what a runtime should do |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | valid | serve |
| `401` | **definite**: unknown, revoked or disabled | stop |
| `503` | we cannot tell right now | retry, keep serving |

A `503` is never a statement about your key: keep serving and retry.

billing_type.description:
The self-hosted product this runtime serves. Always send
the key for the product you run.

user_id.description:
The account this key bills to. A response with no
`user_id` must be treated as a failure — an
identity-less "ok" cannot be billed to anybody.

401.description: Definite — unknown, revoked or disabled key.

503.description:
We cannot validate right now. Retry (a `Retry-After` header is
sent) and keep serving — this is not a statement about your key.

post.summary: Report usage from a self-hosted session
post.description:
The bitHuman SDKs, the CLI and the plugins call this for you: a
self-hosted or on-device session reports its running time here, and
that is what bills it ([Pricing](https://docs.bithuman.ai/pricing)).
You call it only if you build your own runtime.

A report covers the seconds the session ran, idle included, not frames
rendered. The product (`billing_type`) is fixed by the first report of a
session.

Read **only the status code**:

| status | meaning | what a runtime should do |
|---|---|---|
| `2xx` | the interval is recorded | count it as reported |
| `402` | balance depleted / account suspended | **keep rendering**, report it again later |
| `401` | definite bad key | stop |
| `503` | we cannot tell right now | retry |

A `402` never stops a running session; the next session is refused
until you top up. A retried report (same `session_id`, `install_id`
and `seq`) is never charged twice.

session_id.description: Stable id for the session being billed.

seq.description: Beat sequence number within the session.

served_s.description:
Seconds of session covered by this beat. Clamped
server-side; wall-clock, idle included.

billing_type.description:
The self-hosted product wire key. Always send the key
for the product you run.

apiSecret.name: api-secret
apiSecret.description:
Your bitHuman API secret. Get one at
[www.bithuman.ai/developer/api-keys](https://www.bithuman.ai/developer/api-keys).

bearerApiSecret.description:
The same API secret, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <api-secret>`. Self-
hosted runtimes send it this way; the classic `api-secret` header works
on the same routes.

UserId.name: user_id
UserId.description: Your own account id, from `GET /v1/me` (`data.user_id`). Another account's id returns `403 FORBIDDEN`.

SelfHostError.description:
The error envelope the self-hosting routes return. `error.type` is the
machine-readable word a runtime switches on; `error.code`,
`error.httpStatus` and `error.message` are the platform envelope every
other endpoint uses. Both are present on purpose — the self-hosted
container's key validator reads `type`, and the additive `code` means a
developer switching on `error.code` no longer gets `undefined` from
these routes.

upgrade_url.description: On a `plan_required` refusal (403), where to choose a plan.

topup_url.description: On an `insufficient_balance` refusal (402), where to top up credits.

ProviderSelection.description: Which provider one capability uses. `"default"` is the platform's own provider; the object form points the capability at an entry you registered with `PUT /v2/{user_id}/providers`.

provider_id.description: Required when `mode` is `custom`: the `id` of one of your registered provider entries. `providerId` is accepted as a spelling of the same field. An id this account has not registered is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`.

ModelStatusEntry.description: Per-family readiness for one of the agent's models.

state.description: `ready` when the agent can be launched as this family, `pending` while it is still being prepared.

reason.description: Why the family is not ready yet; `null` once it is.
reason.example: this model is still being prepared for this agent

updated_at.description: When this family last changed state. `null` for a family that was available from the agent's creation and never transitioned.

Agent.description: An agent's full record, as returned by `GET /v1/agent/{code}` and `GET /v1/agent/status/{agent_id}`. Every field below is present on every response; fields that do not apply to the agent are `null` rather than absent. `GET /v1/agents` returns a shorter summary — see `AgentListItem`.

code.description: The agent's short code — the primary identifier used across the platform and the embed/viewer URLs.

agent_id.description: The same value as `code`, under the name the creation response uses.

name.description: The agent's display name. **Generated** from the prompt and portrait during the `persona` step — it cannot be supplied at creation or changed afterwards, and it is `null` until that step completes.

description.description: Generated one-paragraph description of the agent. `null` until the `persona` step completes.

model.description: The model family the agent was created with.

supported_models.description: Canonical model families this agent can be launched as right now — `essence-1` when its `.imx` exists, and `essence-2` / `expression-2` once their trained per-identity model has been generated. Tier slugs inherit their family and are not listed.

model_status.description: Readiness per model family, keyed by family name. A family is listed here before it is launchable, with the reason it is not — so a caller can tell "still training" from "never requested". `supported_models` is the `ready` subset of these keys.

subject.description: The subject class the creation classifier recorded for the input, when one was run.

system_prompt.example: You are a friendly fitness coach.

image_path.description: The stored location of the portrait. Same value as `image_url` for agents whose portrait is public.

video_url.description: The agent's identity video URL — generated internally at creation (10 seconds, authored to loop without a seam). Read-only output; video is never a creation input.

video_path.description: The stored location of the identity video. Same value as `video_url` for agents whose video is public.

model_url.description: Where the model artifact lives. For `essence-1` this is a fetchable URL; for the second-generation families it is an opaque stored handle, **not** a link you can download. Use [the download endpoint](#operation/downloadAgentModel) to get the file itself.

model_path.description: The same stored handle as `model_url`, under its storage-side name.

model_hash.description: Content digest of the model artifact, when one has been recorded.

voice_path.description: The same value as `voice_id`, under its storage-side name.

status.description: Current agent state — `processing`, `generating`, `completed`, `success` (all intermediate), `ready` (terminal success) or `failed` (terminal error). `deleted` for a deleted agent.

progress.description: Generation progress as a fraction from 0.0 to 1.0.

error_type.description: Which stage the failure came from; `null` when the agent has not failed.

dynamics.description: Gesture configuration and available gestures. `{}` when none are configured.

AgentListItem.description: One agent as `GET /v1/agents` returns it — a summary, not the full record. Every field below is present on every item; the detail fields (`system_prompt`, `progress`, `model_url`, the media URLs, …) are **not** part of this shape, so read them from `GET /v1/agent/{code}` instead of expecting them here.

name.description: Generated display name; `null` before the persona step and for deleted agents.

status.description: Generation state — `processing`, `generating`, `completed`, `success`, `ready`, `failed` — or `deleted` for an agent you deleted, or `unknown`. **Deleted agents stay in this listing**; filter them out with `?status=ready` or on the field.

supported_models.description: Model families this agent can be launched as right now; `[]` while it is still generating.

model_status.description: Readiness per model family; `{}` while the agent is still generating.

total.description: Total matching rows across all pages.

credits_change.description: Signed credit delta; usage events are positive credits consumed.

events.description: Subscribed event types; empty means all.

secret.description:
HMAC-SHA256 signing secret, returned **only once** at creation.
Verify deliveries with
`sha256 = HMAC(secret, "{X-BitHuman-Timestamp}.{raw_body}")`
and compare against the `X-BitHuman-Signature` header.

status_code.description: HTTP status returned by your endpoint; null on network error/timeout.

upgrade_url.description: On `PLAN_REQUIRED`, `AGENT_LIMIT_REACHED` and `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_REACHED` (403): where to choose a plan. Send the user there instead of retrying. See [Plan and credit refusals](https://docs.bithuman.ai/api/errors#plan-and-credit-refusals).

topup_url.description: On `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` (402): where to top up credits.

BadRequest.description: Missing required parameter or malformed request. The HTTP status equals `status_code` (400).

error.message: Missing required field: text

Unauthorized.description:
Authentication failed. `UNAUTHORIZED` when the `api-secret` header is
present but invalid; `MISSING_AUTH` when it is absent. The HTTP status
equals `status_code` (401).

error.message: Invalid API secret
Agent not found

ValidationError.description: Body failed schema validation. The HTTP status equals `status_code` (400).

error.message: Invalid request parameters

RateLimited.description:
Too many requests. The limiter is **per account** — every API secret on
the account draws from one bucket — and **per cost tier**, so a burst of
reads never uses up your generate budget. Your plan sets the number for
each tier; the matrix, the tier each route belongs to and a retry
recipe are on
[Rate limits](https://docs.bithuman.ai/api/rate-limits).

Wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry. The `X-RateLimit-*` headers let a
client slow down *before* it gets here, but header coverage is uneven
across routes — read them defensively and fall back to exponential
backoff when they are absent.

On a route that can also be called without an API secret, an anonymous
call is metered per network address instead: same body, same
`Retry-After`, no `X-RateLimit-*`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests per minute your plan allows on this request's cost tier.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Whole requests left in the bucket right now.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time at which the bucket is fully refilled.

error.message: Too many generate requests for this api-secret. Retry in ~1s.

RateLimitedByAddress.description:
Too many requests from this network address. These routes carry their
own credential and are checked by the service behind them, so there is
no account to meter at the edge — they get one flat limit per
address (120 requests/minute) instead of the per-plan cost tiers, and
no `X-RateLimit-*` headers. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry. See
[Rate limits](https://docs.bithuman.ai/api/rate-limits).

error.message: Too many requests from this address. Retry in ~1s.

RateLimitedFailedAuth.description:
Too many **failed** key validations from this network address — 30 per
minute. Only failures spend budget, so a runtime presenting a live key
never reaches this, however often it calls. It says nothing about
whether your key is valid: wait `Retry-After` seconds, retry, and read
the answer you get then. See
[Rate limits](https://docs.bithuman.ai/api/rate-limits).

error.message: too many failed validations

EdgeBadGateway.description: Raised by the content delivery network in front of the API, before the request reaches it. **The body is an HTML page, not the JSON envelope every other status uses** — check `Content-Type` before parsing a 5xx. A `Retry-After` header is present, so an ordinary retry helper still works. Any route can answer this.

EdgeGatewayTimeout.description: The request reached the content delivery network in front of the API but no response came back in time. **The body is an HTML page, not the JSON envelope every other status uses** — check `Content-Type` before parsing a 5xx. A `Retry-After` header is present, so an ordinary retry helper still works. Any route can answer this; the long-running routes are the likeliest.

tags.description:

async work finishes (`agent.ready`, `agent.failed`, `video.completed`, `video.failed`). Each
delivery carries an `X-BitHuman-Signature: sha256=<hmac>` header — verify
it with the secret returned once at creation.

tags.description:
Render a finished talking-video mp4 from text or audio. Submit
[`POST /v1/video/generate`](#operation/generateTalkingVideo) — async by
default, or `wait: true` for a blocking render — and poll
[`GET /v1/video/{job_id}`](#operation/getTalkingVideo).

tags.name: Dynamics
tags.description:
Generate and manage conversational gesture animations (wave,
nod, laugh, idle motions) for an avatar. Generate them
asynchronously, then toggle on/off to make them the active model
for live sessions. Gestures trigger based on keyword mapping
during conversation.
